newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF VALENCIA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF VALENCIA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Valencia players ahead of Sunday's Spanish first division match against Barcelona:

Andoni Zubizarreta, goalkeeper, 35. Veteran international with over 550 league games to his name, many of them played with Barcelona. Strong in the air, but prone to moments of clumsiness when forced to clear the ball.

Jorge Bartual, goalkeeper, 25. Despite two solid performances filling in during Zubizarreta's suspension from the UEFA Cup, Bartual does not inspire confidence in his colleagues and Valencia are likely to sign a new keeper for next season.

Jorge Otero, defender, 28. Former Spanish international central defender who has failed to impress this season after earning a place in Spain's Euro 96 squad with a string of fine performances last year.
Jose "Sietes" Suarez, defender, 23. Left-sided defender who has had a poor season and is another player likely to leave the club this year.
Francisco Ferreira, defender, 29. Ferreira is enjoying a fine season in the centre of defence, but is likely to be moved to the left because of an injury crisis.
Fernando Caceres, defender, 27. Former Zaragoza and Boca Juniors central defender who returned to Spain from his native Argentina earlier this season.
Vicente Engonga, defender/midfielder, 31. Born in Spain of Guinean parents. A solid performer who always gives 100 percent.
Gaizka Mendieta, midfielder/defender, 23. Right-sided player who may start the game after a season in which he has hardly played.
Ivan Campo, defender/midfielder, 23. Campo is likely to return to a central defensive role after playing several games in midfield.
Xabier Eskurza, midfielder, 27. Right-sided midfielder who has failed to find a first-team place since arriving from Barcelona two years ago.

Fernando Gomez, midfielder/striker, 31. Former club captain. Has scored over 100 goals and is a favourite with the fans. But Gomez has clashed with coach Jorge Valdano and, despite signs he may end up coaching, Gomez now looks likely to continue his university studies in economics and start a business.
Antonio Poyatos, midfielder, 31. Former Logrones player, the work horse of the Valencia midfield. Earns more than his fair share of yellow cards.
Jose Ignacio Saenz, midfielder, 23. Long-haired midfielder similar in style to Poyatos. Has hardly played this season and is likely to leave Valencia in June.

Claudio Lopez, striker, 23. Left-sided Argentine international who has recently returned from injury. One of the big hopes of the new season, Lopez has had his moments of brilliance but has failed to convince the fans.

Gabriel Moya, striker, 31 on Sunday. Hopes to be back from injury in time to celebrate his birthday with a goal. By failing to celebrate a goal out of respect against his old club, Sevilla, Moya started a trend in the Spanish league.

Leandro, striker, 23. Brazilian who signed from Porto Alegre earlier this season to replace compatriots Viola and Romario. Says he will abandon his dog-cocking-its-leg celebration next time he scores.
